goal: I want more creators to invite their friends.

steps.title: A working invite page that shows the ₹500
steps.why: The invite page only says 'You can invite other creators', its button doesn't do anything, and the ₹500 reward sits in 12px grey text 400px down the screen, so a creator on a phone never sees why they should share.
steps.seen: invite.html: heading 'Invite', the line 'You can invite other creators.', a <button>Copy invite link</button> with no script or link behind it, and the reward line ('when an invited creator finishes their first deal, you both get ₹500') styled margin-top:400px;font-size:12px;color:#999.
steps.build: In invite.html: (1) Change the h1 to 'Invite a friend, you both get ₹500' and directly under it put the reward rule in normal-size text: 'When a friend you invite finishes their first deal, you both get ₹500.' Remove the old grey margin-top:400px paragraph so ₹500 still appears on the page but only near the top. (2) Add a short 3-step list: 'Share your link → Your friend signs up and does a deal → You both get ₹500'. (3) Show the invite link as visible text in a read-only input with id='invite-link'. Build it as signup.html?ref=CODE, taking CODE from ?ref= on the invite page's own URL and falling back to 'friend' if there is none. (4) Make 'Copy invite link' work with a small inline <script> that calls navigator.clipboard.writeText. If that fails, select the input text instead, then change the button label to 'Copied!'. (5) Add a large 'Share on WhatsApp' link above the copy button. Point it at https://wa.me/?text= followed by the URL-encoded message 'Join me on Sunny Shop, brands pay Instagram creators for reels and posts. Sign up with my link and we both get ₹500 after your first deal: <link>'. Keep the nav and style.css. Add tests in test_pages.py: '₹500' appears in invite.html before the button; 'margin-top:400px' is not in invite.html; 'wa.me' and 'signup.html?ref=' are in invite.html; 'clipboard' is in invite.html. Keep test_invite_reward_is_500 passing.

steps.title: A shorter sign-up for invited friends
steps.why: An invite only pays off when the friend finishes a first deal, but sign-up demands 9 things up front, including GST, bank account, IFSC and full address, which many students and part-timers won't have to hand. The terms say PAN is only needed before the first payout.
steps.seen: signup.html: 9 required fields (name as on PAN, email, phone, Instagram, PAN, GST, bank account, IFSC, full postal address) and a 'Submit registration' button. terms.html: 'PAN is required before the first payout.'
steps.build: In signup.html, keep only name, email, phone and Instagram handle as required fields. Move PAN, bank account number, IFSC and address into a section headed 'Payout details (needed before your first payout, you can add these later)'. Remove the 'required' attribute from those fields. Handle GST according to the owner's answer below. Change the h1 to 'Join Sunny Shop as a creator' and the button text to 'Join and see deals'. Add a hidden input name='ref'. Fill it from the ?ref= URL parameter with a small inline script, so the person who invited them can be credited. Keep action='dashboard.html' and the email/instagram field names, which the existing tests check. Add tests: name='gst' is not marked required; name='account' and name='ifsc' are not marked required; name='ref' is in signup.html; signup still goes to dashboard.html.

steps.title: Welcome invited friends with what they'll earn
steps.why: A friend who follows an invite only sees a plain registration form, and the home page talks about 'the future of commerce', not what a creator gets, so the invite has nothing to back it up when the friend clicks.
steps.seen: signup.html: the heading 'Creator registration' and the form, with no word on pay or deals. index.html: 'Sunny Shop is a platform… deliver value' with nothing for creators. deals.html: real paid examples (Chai Co ₹3,000 for 2 reels, Kurta House ₹1,500, FitBottle ₹2,000) that a new visitor never sees
steps.build: In signup.html, above the form, add a short banner that the inline script shows only when ?ref= is in the URL: 'Your friend invited you. Finish your first deal and you both get ₹500.' Under the banner, for everyone, add 2–3 lines with real examples copied from deals.html: 'Brands pay creators like you, e.g. Chai Co ₹3,000 for 2 reels, FitBottle ₹2,000 for 3 stories.' Add the earnings line only if the owner chooses that below. Keep it to a few lines so the form stays near the top on a phone. Add tests: '₹500' and 'Chai Co' appear in signup.html; the 'ref' handling script is present.
